headline_draft: Lenny's Podcast: How I AI — testing TypeSafe AI's Jev on real product workflows
summary: In a solo episode published September 28, 2026, Claire (presumably from the How I AI series) tests Jev, a new decision model from TypeSafe AI that returns structured choices, scores, and probabilities instead of generated text. She runs it against real PM tasks: analyzing 1,700 pull requests for 9 cents, mapping tool usage, triaging 200,000+ email classifications for $4 total cost. The episode demonstrates how structured classification models change the unit economics of data-heavy workflows. She also benchmarks Jev against Claude and explains why it works best alongside a frontier model for decision-making and filtering rather than replacing them.
why_pm: If you're doing user research, feedback analysis, or taxonomy work, Jev shows how small, fast, cheap models can handle high-volume classification at a fraction of frontier-model cost—freeing your research budget to go deeper on insight synthesis rather than raw data processing.
key_facts: Jev is TypeSafe AI's structured decision model
Returns structured data (choices, scores, probabilities) instead of generated text
Works best paired with frontier models like Claude, not as a standalone replacement
quotes: She uses it to analyze 1,700 pull requests for 9 cents, map her Claude and Codex usage, triage email, search 4,500 YouTube comments, and process 200,000 classifications for about $4.

sources.label: Lenny's Podcast: How I AI — Testing Jev on real PM workflows

headline_draft: AI product explainability is now essential — products evaluated by AI before humans ever interact with them
summary: Amy Mitchell, writing on the 2026 PM landscape, argues that a fundamental shift is underway: products are now evaluated by AI systems (in search, recommendations, comparisons, buying guides) before people ever interact with them. This means product *explainability*—how clearly a product communicates its purpose, value, behavior, and limits to *both* people and AI systems—is becoming a core PM responsibility. Keeping product knowledge bases aligned with the product itself is no longer a nice-to-have. Teams failing to expose product features as structured, machine-readable data face a hidden discoverability problem: AI systems will simply describe their products inaccurately to end users.
why_pm: You need to think about how your product looks to an AI reading it. If your product knowledge base is out of sync with the product, or if your messaging is too vague for an AI system to interpret accurately, customers will hear wrong things about you from ChatGPT, Claude, and search. Structured product metadata is now a PM deliverable.
key_facts: Products increasingly evaluated by AI before human interaction
AI-mediated evaluation happens in search, recommendations, buying guides
Product explainability = how clearly product communicates to AI systems and people
Product knowledge alignment with actual product is essential
Structured, machine-readable product data is now critical for discoverability
quotes: Products are increasingly evaluated by AI systems before people ever interact with them. Search, recommendations, comparisons, and even buying guidance now happen through AI-mediated answers.
When explainability is strong, products are represented accurately even without human mediation.

sources.label: Amy Mitchell: 2026 Trends in Product Management
